review_prompts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Asset type: paired macOS app icon and logo direction board, landscape about 3:2.
Create a polished, restrained design review board titled exactly "01 — CRT FAMILY".
Input image 1 is the user's EXISTING Lean VS Code app icon: emerald beveled CRT-like rounded square with a vivid green pixel >_ prompt. This is an identity reference and, for the LEFT icon, the mark to preserve. This direction transfers that existing icon to the terminal product.
Use a warm off-white presentation background and consistent elegant sans-serif typography. Show TWO equal large macOS app icons: LEFT "Lean Term", RIGHT "Lean VS Code".
LEFT: reproduce the reference icon faithfully and unchanged in concept: emerald CRT casing, dark screen, green pixel >_ glyph, exact distinctive existing silhouette and material. RIGHT: create its beautiful companion for a code editor: same casing proportions, bezel, restrained depth, lighting and tactile CRT material, but a cooler deep-teal casing and mint/cyan glowing large solid CURLY BRACES { } as the central glyph. The braces must be bold, widely separated and recognizable, never a chevron or terminal prompt. Do not put >_ on the editor.
Beneath each icon show a compact matching flat symbol plus the exact product name as a clean wordmark treatment, "Lean Term" and "Lean VS Code". Use the same typography for both.
At the bottom show the two icons directly adjacent in small Dock-scale previews on a light gray strip and a dark charcoal strip, each pair at the same scale. Keep their symbols consistent across large and small versions. Let shape, not just color, distinguish the products.
Highly legible and premium, no extra badges, decorative lines, screenshots, stock app logos, explanatory paragraphs or tiny UI chrome. No Microsoft/VS Code ribbon logo. This is a concept board for review, not an installed app screenshot.

Create a polished, restrained design review board titled exactly "03 — FRESH MINIMAL FAMILY".
Input image 1 is a STYLE AND BRAND HERITAGE REFERENCE ONLY: the user's existing emerald CRT >_ app icon. This direction redesigns BOTH app icons with a cleaner modern family, keeping the green Lean brand character while reducing texture and visual noise.

The terminal symbol is asymmetrical; the editor symbol is symmetrical. Keep the braces thick and widely separated. No >_ on the editor. The two must remain distinguishable in grayscale and at small sizes, not solely by green versus blue.

final_editor_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / logo-brand.
Create ONE final production macOS application icon for "Lean VS Code", square 1024 by 1024 canvas, with genuine alpha transparency outside the rounded icon. No presentation board, words, labels, other icons, background scene or cast shadow extending far beyond the icon.
Input image 1 is the exact existing emerald CRT app icon and the geometry/material reference. Input image 2 is the APPROVED "01 — CRT FAMILY" concept board; its RIGHT-HAND teal curly-brace icon is the selected design.
Preserve image 1's rounded-square outer shape, generous macOS icon padding, bevel construction, recessed dark glass screen, restrained grain, crisp highlights at upper left, depth and excellent material quality.
Replace the central green >_ prompt with TWO large bold pixel-style CURLY BRACES { }, matching the RIGHT icon on approved board 2. Make the braces bright mint/cyan, thick, symmetrical, widely separated, and readable at 32 pixels. They must clearly be curly braces, not parentheses or chevrons. Remove the underscore completely.
Change the casing from emerald green to deep blue-teal, as in the approved board, with cool teal edge illumination and a near-black teal screen. Keep the family resemblance to the original emerald icon unmistakable.
Balanced central glyph, approximately the same visual weight as the original >_. No tiny code lines, badges, letters, decorative marks or Microsoft VS Code ribbon. Smooth clean alpha boundary and production-quality edges. Output only the single finished editor app icon.
terminal_source: Exact inherited icon from the installed Lean VS Code app, reassigned with user approval.
